metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Barrackville, WV | Marion County
metaDescription: Marion County mineral owner near Barrackville? We buy coal-era severed mineral interests and gas royalty tied to old family land, with a real title check first.
heroLead: Barrackville grew up alongside the coal seams and gas wells that riddle this stretch of Marion County, which means most mineral ownership here was severed from the surface long before anyone in the family remembers signing anything.
intro: Marion County's mineral history runs through coal first and gas second, and Barrackville sits close to both legacies. Deeds here often reserved coal, oil, and gas in separate clauses written decades apart, so a single tract can carry multiple severed estates with different owners entirely.
We buy oil and gas mineral and royalty interests around Barrackville by working from the actual recorded severance language, not a family's general sense of what they own.

sections.heading: Coal-era severance complicates gas ownership
paragraphs: A lot of Barrackville-area deeds from the early 1900s reserved coal to one party while leaving oil and gas with another, or reserved all minerals together and then split them again at the next sale. Figuring out who actually owns the gas rights under a given tract sometimes takes tracing three or four generations of deed reservations back through the Marion County Clerk's office.

sections.heading: Modern leasing on old severed tracts
paragraphs: Marion County has seen active Marcellus and shallower gas leasing over the past two decades, and severed mineral owners around Barrackville are often surprised to learn a lease or unit order already touches their tract because a prior owner, or an heir they've never met, signed on behalf of a fractional share.

sections.heading: What we do differently
paragraphs: Before we make an offer, we pull the deed book and page for your tract, confirm the severance actually reserved oil and gas rather than coal alone, and check whether an active lease or pooling order already covers it. That means our number reflects what you actually own, not a rough guess.

faqs.question: My deed only mentions coal. Do I still own the gas rights?
faqs.answer: It depends on the exact reservation language. Some deeds severed coal alone; others severed all minerals together, so we read the actual clause before assuming either way.

faqs.question: Is my interest already leased without my knowledge?
faqs.answer: It's possible if a co-owner or predecessor in title signed on behalf of the tract. We check recorded leases and pooling orders in Marion County as part of our review.

faqs.question: What documents do you need to make an offer?
faqs.answer: A copy of any deed, will, or lease you have is helpful, but we can usually locate the recorded chain of title ourselves once we have your name and the tract description.
